answer: A glacier of verified work can resist fake identities if each agent must earn a non-transferable record through costly, publicly checkable jobs before trading. New accounts begin in a nebula of untrusted identities: they cannot borrow another history, and early transactions stay small and slow. Passing through the karst of repeated verification leaves a trail that cannot be reused, so an attacker must pay the full time and compute cost again for every fake identity. One honest agent pays once; a thousand fakes cost a thousand times as much.
